    GDP and Construction Pipeline Example

    gdp-construction.Rmd

    This vignette shows the tsflow CSV workflow end to end:

    • define a pipeline in CSV
    • inspect it with plan_pipeline()
    • inspect the dependency DAG
    • execute it with injected ts inputs

    Example Pipeline

    The package installs a small example mapping as CSV together with a sidecar metadata file. tsflow reads the CSV, merges the sibling metadata, and compiles the result into the same structured pipeline model used by the YAML format.

    example_path <- system.file("examples", "gdp_construction.csv", package = "tsflow")
cat(paste(readLines(example_path), collapse = "\n"))
#> name,input,step_1,step_2,unit
#> gdp.nominal.quarterly,gdp.nominal.quarterly.sa,"jsa(gdp.nominal.annual.nsa, method=@jsa_method)",,
#> construction.nominal.quarterly,construction.nominal.annual,"a2q_sum(gdp.nominal.quarterly, conversion=@conversion)",,div(1000000)
#> construction.real.quarterly,construction.growth.annual,"real_gr_nom(construction.nominal.annual, base_year=@base_year)","a2q_sum(gdp.nominal.quarterly, conversion=@conversion)",
#> construction.deflator.quarterly,construction.nominal.quarterly,div(construction.real.quarterly),,mul(100)
    meta_path <- system.file("examples", "gdp_construction.meta.yml", package = "tsflow")
cat(paste(readLines(meta_path), collapse = "\n"))
#> vars:
#>   jsa_method: denton-cholette
#>   base_year: 2015
#>   conversion: sum

    Define Transforms

    This example uses real R functions with the same calling style that tsflow expects at execution time. They are defined in the vignette environment so they can be resolved by name during planning and execution.

    library(tsflow)

jsa <- function(
  ts_sa,
  ts_nsa,
  method = "uniform",
  conversion = "sum"
) {
    ts_nsa_a <- tempdisagg::ta(ts_nsa, conversion = conversion, to = "annual")

    if (method == "denton-cholette") {
        return(tempdisagg::td(
            ts_nsa_a ~ 0 + ts_sa,
            method = "denton-cholette",
            criterion = "additive",
            h = 1
        )$values)
    }

    tempdisagg::td(
        ts_nsa_a ~ ts_sa,
        conversion = conversion,
        to = "quarterly",
        method = method
    )$values
}

real_gr_nom <- function(ts_gr, ts_nom, base_year) {
    ts_gr <- zoo::na.trim(ts_gr)
    if (frequency(ts_gr) < frequency(ts_nom)) {
        ts_nom <- tempdisagg::ta(
            ts_nom,
            conversion = "sum",
            to = frequency(ts_gr)
        )
    }

    ts_real <- ts(
        NA,
        start = start(ts_gr) - c(1, 0),
        end = end(ts_gr),
        frequency = frequency(ts_gr)
    )

    base_year_value <- as.numeric(window(
        ts_nom,
        start = c(base_year, 1),
        end = c(base_year, 1)
    ))
    window(ts_real, start = c(base_year, 1), end = c(base_year, 1)) <- base_year_value

    product_up <- (ts_gr / 100 + 1)
    if (base_year < end(ts_gr)[1]) {
        up_vals <- as.numeric(window(product_up, start = c(base_year + 1, 1)))
        window(ts_real, start = c(base_year + 1, 1)) <- base_year_value * cumprod(up_vals)
    }

    product_down <- 1 / product_up
    if (base_year > start(ts_gr)[1]) {
        down_vals <- as.numeric(window(product_down, end = c(base_year, 1)))
        window(ts_real, end = c(base_year - 1, 1)) <- rev(base_year_value * cumprod(rev(down_vals)))
    }

    ts_real
}

a2q_sum <- function(ts_d, indicator, conversion = "sum") {
    ts_d <- zoo::na.trim(ts_d)
    indicator <- zoo::na.trim(indicator)

    start_td <- max(stats::time(indicator)[1], stats::time(ts_d)[1])
    end_td <- utils::tail(stats::time(indicator), 1)

    indicator <- window(indicator, start = start_td, end = end_td)

    if (any(!is.na(ts_d)) && any(!is.na(indicator))) {
        return(tempdisagg::td(
            ts_d ~ indicator,
            conversion = conversion,
            to = "quarterly",
            method = "chow-lin-maxlog"
        )$values)
    }

    tempdisagg::td(
        ts_d ~ 1,
        conversion = conversion,
        to = "quarterly",
        method = "denton-cholette"
    )$values
}

    Plan The Pipeline

    Plan the pipeline before running it:

    plan <- plan_pipeline(
    path = example_path,
    transform_env = environment()
)

plan
#> <PipelinePlan>
#>   nodes: 8
#>   outputs: 4
#>   execution order: 8
#>   output names: gdp.nominal.quarterly, construction.nominal.quarterly, construction.real.quarterly, construction.deflator.quarterly
plan$dag$order
#> [1] "gdp.nominal.quarterly.sa"        "gdp.nominal.annual.nsa"         
#> [3] "construction.nominal.annual"     "construction.growth.annual"     
#> [5] "gdp.nominal.quarterly"           "construction.nominal.quarterly" 
#> [7] "construction.real.quarterly"     "construction.deflator.quarterly"
dag_edges(plan$dag, include_labels = TRUE)
#>                             from                              to
#> 1       gdp.nominal.quarterly.sa           gdp.nominal.quarterly
#> 2         gdp.nominal.annual.nsa           gdp.nominal.quarterly
#> 3    construction.nominal.annual  construction.nominal.quarterly
#> 4          gdp.nominal.quarterly  construction.nominal.quarterly
#> 5     construction.growth.annual     construction.real.quarterly
#> 6    construction.nominal.annual     construction.real.quarterly
#> 7          gdp.nominal.quarterly     construction.real.quarterly
#> 8 construction.nominal.quarterly construction.deflator.quarterly
#> 9    construction.real.quarterly construction.deflator.quarterly
#>                 label
#> 1          jsa: ts_sa
#> 2         jsa: ts_nsa
#> 3       a2q_sum: ts_d
#> 4  a2q_sum: indicator
#> 5  real_gr_nom: ts_gr
#> 6 real_gr_nom: ts_nom
#> 7  a2q_sum: indicator
#> 8           div: left
#> 9          div: right

    If igraph and visNetwork are installed, you can inspect the DAG interactively in the HTML vignette:

    dag_to_visnetwork(plan, upstream_of = "construction.deflator.quarterly")
    Click a node to inspect the upstream calculation path.

    Execute The Pipeline

    Raw inputs are injected as named ts objects. The vignette uses a small packaged dataset for this step:

    data("gdp_construction_inputs", package = "tsflow")
inputs <- gdp_construction_inputs

result <- execute_pipeline(
    path = example_path,
    inputs = inputs,
    transform_env = environment()
)
#> High frequency series shorter than low frequency. Discarding low frequency before 2010.

    result$values contains the full executed state. Because the example CSV does not define explicit outputs, result$outputs defaults to the derived series:

    names(result$outputs)

    You can also execute only the subgraph needed for one target:

    constr_nom_result <- execute_pipeline(
    path = example_path,
    inputs = inputs,
    outputs = "construction.nominal.quarterly",
    transform_env = environment()
)

    On Linux, you can evaluate the same subgraph with a parallel future backend:

    oplan <- future::plan()
on.exit(future::plan(oplan), add = TRUE)
future::plan(future::multicore, workers = 2)

output <- execute_pipeline(
  path = example_path,
  inputs = inputs,
  outputs = "construction.nominal.quarterly",
  transform_env = environment()
)
